economy.note: US 10-Year and Gold as of 4:00 PM ET April 27th; WTI Crude reflects today's intraday move via investing.com.
economy.commentary:
The 10-year sat dead flat ahead of tomorrow's Fed announcement. Bond market is in wait-and-see mode.

Gold ticked up marginally near record highs.

WTI ripped +3.2% to $99.43, with Brent pushing past $108 (about 50% above pre-war levels). Iran sent Trump a proposed deal: end the U.S. Blockade of Hormuz and pause nuclear talks. Experts say Trump is unlikely to accept. U.S. Average gas hit $4.11/gal (up 7 cents in a week), diesel at $5.45. Diesel pricing typically shows up in grocery prices a few weeks later, so watch for the inflation echo into the rate decision.

BofA raised 2026 GDP forecast to 2.8% (from 2.6%) on stronger spending and credit data. The catch: stronger growth makes Fed cuts harder to justify.

crypto.note: Numbers as of 4:00 PM ET on April 27th.
crypto.commentary:
Crypto pulled back across the board. The bigger story: DeFi platforms got drained for $605M+ in the first 20 days of April alone. Kelp DAO lost $293M on April 19; Solana's Drift Protocol lost $285M on April 1. Aave (largest DeFi lender) froze some markets, and its own coin is down 20% on the contagion.

Meanwhile, spot Bitcoin ETFs pulled in $18.7B in Q1 (BlackRock's IBIT led with $8.4B). Total ETF crypto assets now exceed $128B. The takeaway: institutional money is choosing the regulated wrapper over the underlying tokens. Self-custody is losing the retail vote.

real_estate.homebuilder: Real Brokerage Buys RE/MAX in $880M Deal; Cloud Brokerages Eat the Franchise Model
real_estate.commentary:
The brokerage industry just consolidated again. The Real Brokerage (REAX -24.63%) is buying RE/MAX (RMAX +23.68%) in an $880M deal, creating "Real REMAX Group" with 180,000+ agents across 120 countries. This is the second major brokerage M&A in seven months after Compass's $1.6B Anywhere Real Estate buyout. The signal: cloud-first brokerages are absorbing the legacy franchise model, and the market punished Real (-24%) for what it sees as overpaying. For agents at any independent or boutique brokerage, the question is no longer "if" your platform consolidates but "when."

Renters just got leverage too. Nearly 40% of U.S. Rental listings now come with concessions (free month, waived fees), rent growth slowed to 1.8% YoY (weakest pace since 2020), and building permits have been falling since 2022. That's the bottom of the housing demand stack softening, which eventually pulls starter-home demand with it if rates don't move.

The Fed lands tomorrow (Wednesday). The cross-currents: BofA just raised 2026 GDP to 2.8% (makes a cut harder), while consumer confidence sits at an all-time low and WTI surged +3.2% on Iran-Hormuz tension (makes a cut more urgent).
